chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Muḥriz, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
He wrote to me from the prison: “So-and-so, my son, is the chief of my children, and I have bestowed my teknonym upon him.”

key_terms.ابْنِي: my son; indicating the Imam’s direct reference to his son
key_terms.الْحَبْسِ: imprisonment; the place from which the Imam عليه السلام sent the written statement
key_terms.سَيِّدُ: chief or master; denoting preeminence and distinction
key_terms.كُنْيَتِي: my teknonym; the honorific appellation granted to the son
key_terms.نَحَلْتُهُ: I bestowed upon him; indicating a grant or conferment
key_terms.وُلْدِي: my children; the Imam’s offspring among whom one is singled out

ai.seo_question: What did Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام write from prison about his son’s status among his children?
ai.summary: This report records a written statement from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while in prison, identifying one of his sons as the foremost among his children. The wording also indicates distinction and designation through granting him his kunyah, which reflects status and recognition within the family line.
